title: EtaleLimitInjectiveColimitAcyclic
statement: Let $I$ be a nonempty directed preordered set and let $D:I^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{Sch}$ be an inverse diagram of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] with affine transition morphisms. Let $(X,(f_i))$ be a limit cone [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. For each $i$, let $F_i$ be an abelian sheaf on $(D_i)_{\acute{e}t}$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], with maps $\varphi_f:D(f^{\mathrm{op}})^{-1}F_i\to F_j$ for $f:i\to j$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] satisfying the canonical inverse-image identity and composition laws. Let $G:I\to\operatorname{Ab}(X_{\acute{e}t})$ be identified objectwise with $f_i^{-1}F_i$ by isomorphisms, its arrows being inverse-image composition followed by pullback of $\varphi_f$. Let $L$ be a colimit cocone on $G$, with coprojections $\iota_i$.  Assume in addition that every $F_i$ is injective in its abelian sheaf category. Then for every $n\ge0$, $H^{n+1}(X,L)$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology] is zero, expressed as Subsingleton. This assertion concerns any compatible injective system, and does not construct a replacement or a boundary map. Here an object A is injective if every map into A extends across every monomorphism. A short exact sequence means its first arrow is monic, its second is epic, and the first image equals the second kernel [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence]. The morphism of short complexes consists of three coefficient maps commuting with their two differentials.

source.place: Step 3 of the parent acyclic-replacement plan: injective Cech complexes and degree-zero continuity imply positive cohomology vanishing. Tags 09YN and 09YQ identify the scheme-site realization.

proof.text: Use the qcqs etale basis on the limit. Descend each finite affine covering and its object to a stage using the affine-site colimit presentation. On a cofinal tail all its iterated covering fibre products are qcqs systems. Apply the full degree-zero section comparison from 09YN (including its equality criterion) on each, with the same prescribed units; finite products give the Cech-complex colimit. The stage injective Cech complexes are positively acyclic, exact filtered group colimits preserve this, and cofinal finite qcqs coverings permit the Cech criterion. Thus LE has zero positive object cohomology at every qcqs object, including the terminal object. This step uses no higher-degree continuity.
Apply the positive object-cohomology vanishing to the terminal small etale object and degree n+1. Restriction to a cofinal finite qcqs basis does not change this global cohomology.

theorem etale_limit_injective_colimit_acyclic
    {I : Type u} [Preorder I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)] [Nonempty I]
    (D : Iᵒᵖ ⥤ Scheme.{u}) (c : Cone D) (hc : IsLimit c)
    [∀ i : Iᵒᵖ, CompactSpace (D.obj i)] [∀ i : Iᵒᵖ, QuasiSeparatedSpace (D.obj i)]
    [∀ (i j : Iᵒᵖ) (f : i ⟶ j), IsAffineHom (D.map f)]
    (F : ∀ i : I, Sheaf (D.obj (op i)).smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})
    (φ : ∀ {i j : I} (f : i ⟶ j),
      (upperStar AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} (D.map f.op)).obj (F i) ⟶ F j)
    (hidentity : ∀ i : I, φ (𝟙 i) =
      (eqToIso (congrArg (upperStar AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}) (D.map_id (op i)))).hom.app
        (F i) ≫ (upperStarId AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} (D.obj (op i))).hom.app (F i))
    (hcomposition : ∀ (i j k : I) (f : i ⟶ j) (g : j ⟶ k),
      φ (f ≫ g) =
        (upperStarComp AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} (D.map g.op) (D.map f.op)
          (D.map (f ≫ g).op) (D.map_comp g.op f.op)).hom.app (F i) ≫
        (upperStar AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} (D.map g.op)).map (φ f) ≫ φ g)
    (G : I ⥤ Sheaf c.pt.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})
    (eG : ∀ i : I, G.obj i ≅
      (upperStar AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} (c.π.app (op i))).obj (F i))
    (hG : ∀ (i j : I) (f : i ⟶ j), G.map f =
      (eG i).hom ≫
        (upperStarComp AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} (c.π.app (op j)) (D.map f.op)
          (c.π.app (op i)) (c.w f.op).symm).hom.app (F i) ≫
        (upperStar AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} (c.π.app (op j))).map (φ f) ≫ (eG j).inv)
    (L : Cocone G) (hL : IsColimit L)
    (hinj : ∀ i : I, Injective (F i)) (n : ℕ) :
    Subsingleton (Sheaf.H L.pt (n + 1))
